A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Compositional-ARC study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model comparisons, experiments across four data splits, component ablations, and a static-grammar training control in Tables 1–2 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original error analyses and evaluation on a dataset with more varied transformations in Sections 5.2–5.3.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the 5.7M-parameter encoder-decoder, patch encoding, positional embeddings, auxiliary copy task, and background-weighted loss. v3 applies the same method to broader transformation coverage; Appendix C.3 explains its existing differences from the original linguistic MLC.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds an evaluated variant allowing one- or two-cell translations in all four directions, extensions in all directions, and yellow/green recoloring alongside red/orange. v2 evaluates only the narrower transformation choices. The spatial domain, grid size, five transformation families, and composition depth remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, o3-mini, the two ARC-specific LLMs and their existing variants, and the static-grammar seq2seq control. Models and prompting methods introduced in the expanded literature review are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds a seven-category error-coding procedure and a separate split for the broader dataset, while retaining the original evaluation settings. Appendix B.3 clarifies existing split construction rather than changing it. The new experiment's sample count is unresolved: Table 8 lists 85,528/5,472/5,473 training/validation/test episodes, totaling 96,473, whereas Section 5.3 states 100,000.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, split-consistency checks, static-grammar control, and qualitative examples, v3 adds systematic failure-mode analysis across models. Section 5.2 and Tables 5–6 distinguish copying, partial compositions, formatting, and spatial errors, with indicator-level breakdowns. Section 5.3 additionally tests sensitivity to increased transformation diversity.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same four-split means and standard deviations in Table 2 and the same run and seed descriptions. v3 removes duplicated standard deviations from the ablation prose but preserves them in the table. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, ablation, response-validity, and static-control results remain unchanged. v3 adds 88.10% exact-match, 99.83% color, and 88.25% shape accuracy on the broader dataset. Tables 5–6 add substantial diagnostic findings: for example, invalid shapes account for 70.57% of MLC errors, while level-1 predictions account for 71.55% of Mistral's errors after test-time training. These are additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The substantive grid, object, transformation, and evaluation-metric definitions and equations remain unchanged after renumbering. v3's new boxed Definition 1 restates the existing systematic-generalization concept using primitive symbols; it introduces no substantive mathematical assumptions, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and central conclusion retain the same claims: a spatial systematicity benchmark, successful MLC generalization beyond language, superiority to the evaluated general-purpose LLMs, and performance comparable to the ARC-winning model with test-time training. The additions support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly identifies fixed-size grids and restricted transformations as limitations, acknowledges uncertainty about more complex ARC problems, and proposes learned problem decomposition as future work. Appendix A also qualifies LLM systematicity failures by discussing abilities elicited through decomposition and compositional training.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the random 80/20 transformation-triplet partition and subsequent validation/test division, and supplies a direct dataset access location. Appendix C.3 adds reference MLC training details and contrasts them with this work. Existing implementation settings, hardware, timings, prompts, and code access remain available.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning through literature on algorithmic tasks, mathematical traps, semantic parsing, instruction composition, morphology, and training-data coverage. Added works include Drozdov et al., Thomm et al., Chang et al., and Wold et al. The review contrasts systematicity failures with successful decomposition-based prompting and data-centric explanations.

P1.justification: Existing prose and section order are largely retained, with light editing, updated author/contact and conference-header text, and clearer explanations. New results subsections, an appendix review, a training comparison, and a limitations paragraph extend the narrative without extensive rewriting of existing material.

P2.justification: v3 adds a quantitative error-distribution figure and detailed error tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation of model behavior. It also adds the broader-dataset statistics table, redraws Figure 1's connectors and spacing, and specifies the visual grammar in Figure 3's caption. Existing benchmark and example displays are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's existing benchmark and ablation evidence, v3 improves diagnostic understanding, tests broader transformation coverage, and clarifies limitations, research context, and reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains. The added coverage experiment reports only one split, and its episode totals conflict between Section 5.3 and Table 8, limiting confidence in its documentation without undermining the retained results.
